rules: Live check 4 runs after sub-run C6 is merged and pushed, CI and the Desktop app workflow are green on that head, and in a session started after the owner's 2026-11-09 token update (FORERUNNER_TEST_GITHUB_TOKEN). Live check 3 (wave 15, cap USD 3) runs on run B's merged head before C1, as planned: its G2 builds two projects on one repository, which D1 forbids from C2 on.

Cap USD 7.00, raised on 2026-11-15 for run L3's step LC-L3 (estimate USD 7.05 for every step; USD 4.37 at priority 1, USD 2.68 at priority 2): priority 1 first in the listed order, then priority 2 in the listed order while the ledger is under USD 6.30 (no new step after USD 6.30), priority 3 last; a step not reached goes to the owner's checklist or the next leftovers; no step is repeated at this cap. Amended 2026-11-16 (C4b's LC-C32, USD 0.15 at priority 1): estimate USD 7.20 for every step, USD 4.52 at priority 1; the cap and the order rules are unchanged, so LC-L3 (the last priority 2 step) is likely not reached and its parts go to the owner's checklist or the leftovers as this rule says. The send-back ('fixes') half cannot be forced with the real critic: it is checked on the bench and in the composed tests, and live only if the real critic sends a task back.

Steps with after_sub_run C2, C4 or C5 cost no model money and may run as soon as that sub-run is merged (early warning before the next sub-run builds on it): LC-C1 after C2 (Work together and the take-over on forerunner-sandbox in two bench homes; the sandbox's leftover bench pull requests #1, #2, #3, #6 and #7 were closed with the owner's yes on 2026-11-09 20:10 UTC), LC-C4 after C4 (Make one project on GitHub), LC-C20 after C5 (the Desktop app workflow's window job on the pushed C5 head, read again after C6) and LC-C31 after C5 (the continuation, no spend; the preset set through settings.set credential_policy, its Settings screen after C6). A failure found early becomes a fix note for the next sub-run's fixers (args.fixNotes) instead of waiting for C6.

Every step uses FORERUNNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the bench start (--provider bench-live) or in the live harness, never printed, logged or committed; GitHub steps write only to forerunner-sandbox and the person closes what they open.

steps.step:
LC-C32 (d1116-budget-all, the owner's answer of 2026-11-16: a task's budget counts its review): A task's own budget counts its review (the owner's answer of 2026-11-16), on the API key with the real critic, in LC-C18's bench home after LC-C18 (priority 1, after C6). The budgets come from computed figures. On Sonnet 5.5 the critic's first call is admitted on about USD 0.10 (8,192 output tokens are USD 0.082). The coder's first step is about USD 0.06 (4,096 output tokens are USD 0.041), and the footer's work is about USD 0.02 to 0.04. So CHF 0.10 (USD 0.125) lets the work run and leaves about what the review's first call needs: either branch can happen. CHF 1.00 keeps a room. The session lead may move the first budget from the fix's bench walk record (the coder's and the critic's first-call estimates).
1. With --provider bench-live (FORERUNNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, never printed), in a folder project, press New task twice:
   - task A: a coder task 'Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html' with Budget 0.10;
   - task B: a coder task 'Add a contact line with the club's email to index.html' with Budget 1.00.
2. Read the Start dialog's figures and any line about a review that may wait, then press Start.
3. Watch the session log, the Tasks rows and the drawers.
4. If a card comes for A, answer Continue (CHF N more) once.
5. Open Costs > By task and both drawers.
6. Save the model-call log, the ledger rows per task, and each critic call's estimate (model_call_start's estimateUsdMicro, or the refusal kept on the card).
Pass if:
- A's Start dialog figure is at most CHF 0.10 and includes a review (above A's work-only figure from the bench walk). If BA-12 was built, the dialog says A's review may wait.
- B's start line reads 'This run may spend CHF x (CHF y of the task's budget is kept for its review): ...'. B is reviewed with no refusal and is done within CHF 1.00. A's start line has no such clause.
- Exactly one of these holds for A, and the record says which:
  - (i) A's review fits: A is done, its row reads its cost with 'of CHF 0.10 budget', and the ledger's sum for A is at most CHF 0.10.
  - (ii) A's review waits: the log says '"Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html" paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.10 has no room for it.', and the session goes on (B runs and is reviewed; no 'Stopped at this session's budget'). The Inbox has one card: title '"Add a footer line with the club's name to index.html" paused at its budget of CHF 0.10', body 'The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.', and Continue (CHF N more), with N at least the refused call's estimate plus the review's part less what was left. Before Continue the ledger's sum for A is at most CHF 0.10. After Continue: one session, critic calls only and no coder call, A done, no second card.
  - (iii) A's work pauses at its budget: a work-pause card with Continue, and after Continue the coder runs once more and then the critic.
- For each task, the row, the drawer and Costs > By task show one figure, equal to the ledger's sum for the task, reviews included. No screen says 'reviews are not counted'.
- If the real critic sends either task back, the next run's start line follows the room rule, and the task's ledger never passes its budget before a Continue. If not, the record says the send-back was checked only on the bench and by the owner's U-042 step.
- Record each review's real first-call worst case and real cost, for REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ALLOWANCE_TOKENS and the tier 1 review start. C4b leftovers adds (the merge's notes): record what one Continue adds at a tiny budget and whether its button reads as reasonable (C4bL-5: on the stand-in CHF 0.004 gave CHF 0.07 more); whether any real work run passes its work cap (C4bL-2); the waiting review's card and drawer words as C6 built them (C4b-left-6); and, if C6 built it, the Start dialog's line for a budget that may leave too little for its review (C4b-left-5).

steps.step: LC-C31 (the owner's decision of 2026-11-09, (a); no model spend): the bench with the subscription stand-in and this environment's real API key saved second (never printed), preset 'Subscription first, then wait' (set through settings.set credential_policy after C5; its Settings screen comes in C6); a person's two-task session whose second task meets the stand-in's limit. Expect: the first task done, the session ending to wait, GET /running and the bar '<project> · waiting until <time>, then it goes on' with Cancel; zero requests to api.anthropic.com during the wait (the harness's request log); at the stand-in's reset exactly one session by 'continuation' with the budget left (the ledger) on the stand-in, its log 'Goes on with your session of <time>.'; quit and start the daemon once during the wait: still one continuation; a second run with Cancel pressed: nothing starts at the reset and the rows read 'Ready: it runs at your next Start.'; a third run with quiet hours set to cover the stand-in's reset: the bar names the end of the quiet hours and the session goes on once then; a fourth with Stop after this task pressed before the stop: the session ends without a continuation and nothing starts at the reset; while one waits, Start on that project answers 'Your session of <time> goes on by itself at <time>.' and starts nothing. A fifth run on a home where nothing was ever chosen: chat, a review and the task's planning make their calls on the subscription stand-in and none on the key (the default preset for every call, the owner's answer 4). C3 adds: the continuation's first log line is 'Goes on with your session of HH:MM.'; while the credential rests, Start reads 'Start at HH:MM' and keeps one start; with quiet hours covering the reset, every line names when the session really goes on; after Cancel the wait, nothing anywhere says the session goes on (C3-left-8). C5 leftovers adds: while the session waits, look at the Overview at 375 px and at 1280 px and record how often the wait and Cancel show (bar, Working now, status line) and whether the status line's Cancel reads clearly with its explanation only as a tooltip (C5L-11: the session lead decides at the triage); after Cancel, ask chat 'what happened last session?' and type 'summary': record whether either still says the session goes on (C5L-15).

steps.step: LC-C27 (d1109-selftasks-run) On the real API key at Standard: a 3-task plan whose first task's real coder run is briefed with the new 'For the task list:' line on a task that is clearly two jobs; check that the real specialist writes the heading, that the real planning model's JSON passes the strict schema first time, that the split and the added step are right and applied with one Undo each, that the new tasks run in the same session when they fit, and the check's cost on the session page (expect about CHF 0.03 to 0.05 a check). C4b adds (d1116-budget-all): After LC-C27's session ends, read the session review's Details and its findings. Pass if: The Details names the task check's spend apart ('the session's own checks CHF z'), and no 'over their estimate' finding comes from the task checks alone. No task's figure includes the check's cost. C4 adds (d1109-selftasks-run's review): the real planning model's reply passes the strict JSON shape first time; each split part carries every criterion; the Details line costs about CHF 0.03 to 0.05; at Assisted the card's body quotes the report once; a plan task only made to wait for an added step has no 'The project's agent wrote this task' line in its brief (C4-left-1); note whether the check's line belongs in the session log (C4L-15) and how often a person-written task gets a card at Standard instead of a fix (the owner's answer 7).

steps.step: LC-C28 (d1109-selftasks-chat) On the real API key at Assisted: chat 'fix the tasks' on a project with a duplicate and a missing step; check the read-back lists the right changes in one line, Yes makes them as one row with one Undo, and the wait line shows while the planning model runs. C6 leftovers adds: the read-back names what each edit changes ('priority to High', never 'reword'); the drawer of an added task reads 'Added by the agent: ...'; the model-call log's task-check request holds the person's line verbatim and its model follows the planning setting (C5-left-7). Leave one read-back open for more than 10 minutes, then answer Yes: record what happens (C6L-11). Also say a change in chat in your own words that the chat model makes (not 'fix the tasks'), and record whether Changes names you or the agent (C6L-10).

steps.step: LC-L3 (run L3's fixes, merged at 7aa7add): run the check_in_the_app steps of run L3's fixed items (40 in /tmp/frbench/runL3-<area>-fix.json and -fixup.json, fixed[].check_in_the_app), folded into the journeys the other steps already make (the GitHub chain on forerunner-sandbox, the research run, the chat, the money screens) so that no step is paid twice. Priority 1 inside it: L3-github-1 (close A on GitHub, press Merge on B before the next look: refused at once, nothing merged, one card), L3-github-2 (cards close when merged on GitHub, through a restart), L3-run-1 (Haiku calls settings_set on 'research may read any public website again' and never claims a confirmation it did not ask for; the reply guard's line if it does), L3-research-1 and L3-research-4 (a finished research run goes to its review; the node --test criterion is checked). The rest at priority 3. Live check 3's model-only items too: the L3-run-1 Haiku settings_set behaviour and the steps X5 to X9 it skipped at its cap. C4b adds (d1116-budget-all): for L3-run-3, its check_in_the_app steps 3 to 6 are replaced by (priority 3 inside LC-L3, no added cost): 1. In the money-screens journey LC-L3 already makes, press New task: a coder task 'Write the Swiss pairing tool with tests' with Budget 0.20 and criteria that name its files and a test. Read the plan card or Start dialog figure. 2. Start, and let the real critic review. 3. Read the Tasks row, the drawer and the run's start line. At the end, read Costs > By task. Pass if: - The task's figure includes its review and is at most CHF 0.20. - The row reads its cost with 'of CHF 0.20 budget' under it, or 'CHF 0.20 budget used up'. It never reads a cost above CHF 0.20 before a Continue, and never 'reviews are not counted'. - With no room kept at this budget, the start line has no room clause. - The task ends done within CHF 0.20, or paused before its review with the one card and Continue. - If the critic sent it back, the second run's line follows the room rule and the ledger never passes CHF 0.20 before a Continue. - The drawer header and Costs > By task show the row's figure.
